requirements: Adopt a unified action-class policy across Orchestrator/runtime surfaces, classified by confirmation level (none, light, strong, hard_gate) and reversibility (immediate_undo, compensating_action_only, non_reversible).
Keep records and artifacts distinct: canonical structured records in Ledger/export/search, with files/blobs linked as artifacts.
Use record-first exports for exact-record surfaces; treat CSV/table exports as convenience view exports, not archival canon.
Separate settings semantics into three axes: source (inherit/override), requested (run intent), and execution/result (effective plus honored/skipped/clamped).
Keep global requested-Persona precedence while requiring deterministic auto-resolver outputs per surface.
decisions: Strong vs hard_gate confirms are distinct: hard_gate actions must follow runtime-defined non-bypassable allowed-action contracts, not generic modals.
Standardize terminology so Undo is used only for true immediate undo; use Restore/Reopen/Retry for compensating flows.
Define Orchestrator export modes explicitly as record export, bundle export, and view export.
In Persona auto-resolution, actor type and operation type should outrank stack hints.
data_shapes: Shared record envelope: record_id, record_kind, project_id, optional run_id, scoped refs, status, created metadata, supersession link, source_refs, artifact_refs, evidence_refs, summary, optional detail_ref.
Minimum explicit record families: review, corroboration request/result, graph patch request/result, promotion, recovery, and state transition report.
Orchestrator export manifest fields include ids/kind/project/run context, generation timestamp, source surface, filter summary, counts, included ids, status notes, and schema version.
Settings/runtime display grammar fields: Inherited from, Overridden by, Requested, Effective, Reason, Support.
routing_rules: Action family routing: none for safe navigation/read-only UI actions; light for moderate accidental actions; strong for state-destructive or live-execution-changing actions; hard_gate for HITL/runtime-governed approvals and canonical graph-changing gates.
Surface routing for settings data: Settings is source-axis heavy; Orchestrator/inspectors are requested-vs-effective heavy; History/Ledger is immutable audit-heavy.
Auto Persona routing should map role-specific defaults across package/seam overseer, node worker, verifier/reviewer, corroborator, recovery actor, and graph patch planner.
verification_rules: Strong confirmations must include concrete consequences and reversibility class; hard_gate confirmations must include runtime-defined allowed actions and no hidden bypass.
Historical exports/runs must preserve truth even when live backing objects are removed or superseded.
Historical run views must remain frozen to historical requested/effective values.
If same-tier Persona candidates cannot be deterministically resolved, require clarification instead of speculative selection.
owner_consumer_obligations: Expose winning source/origin for effective settings (persona/model/auth/account/worker policy) so users do not reconstruct precedence manually.
Record requested Persona, effective Persona, and selection reason when fallback occurs due to capability/provider constraints.
Preserve lineage metadata when destructive cleanup actions remove live objects.
stale_retirement_items: Retire ambiguous mixed use of revert/rollback/restore/undo and normalize to precise recovery semantics.
Retire implicit assumptions that deleted/pruned objects can be treated as non-historical; keep retired-object metadata exportable.
open_questions: Delete Run semantics remain unresolved (authorization boundary, reversibility, and lineage guarantees).
Orchestrator export contracts still need canonical specificity for packaging records/artifacts/references under superseded or removed backing objects.
Presentation parity for non-Persona manual overrides (provider/model/account/worker policy) is still underdefined.
Orchestrator auto Persona prioritization is still too qualitative without a fully explicit matrix.
process_defects: Confirmation behavior is fragmented across subsystems without one shared action policy matrix.
Exact record families are referenced but incompletely normalized compared with attempts/blocked/usage envelopes.
Orchestrator export language is more UI-view-centric than canonical-contract-centric.
Override presentation consistency is weaker across settings/runtime surfaces than requested/effective runtime recording.
doc_hints: Align action policy and record/export semantics with storage-plan, Orchestrator page, contracts, GUI spec, and run graph documents.
Align settings override and Persona resolution rules across Multi-Account, Models System, Prompt Pipeline, Personas, and Orchestrator integration docs.
